events.region: Northwest Plateau; Chuska Mountains; Far Northwest Highlands; Northwest Highlands; West Central Plateau; West Central Mountains; West Central Highlands; Southwest Mountains; San Francisco River Valley; Tusas Mountains Including Chama; Jemez Mountains
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of north central, northwest, and west central New
Mexico, including the following areas, in north central New Mexico,
Far Northwest Highlands, Jemez Mountains, Northwest Highlands and
Tusas Mountains Including Chama. In northwest New Mexico, Chuska
Mountains and Northwest Plateau. In west central New Mexico, San
Francisco River Valley, Southwest Mountains, West Central
Highlands, West Central Mountains and West Central Plateau.

* WHEN...Through Monday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding may occur
in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water crossings may be
flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Another round of widespread rainfall is expected today into
Monday with rainfall amounts generally between 1 and 2 inches
near and west of the Continental Divide, except near 3 inches in
favored upslope regions of the Tusas Mountains near Chama. This
rainfall will occur over very saturated soils which will increase
runoff. These are also areas that are still recovering from the
last flood event. River rises are likely and some rivers may
flood. If river flooding materializes, it will likely continue
into Monday evening.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.region: Waters from Pensacola FL to Pascagoula MS from 20 to 60 NM
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
SMWMOB

The National Weather Service in Mobile has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Waters from Pensacola FL to Pascagoula MS from 20 to 60 NM...

* Until 800 AM CST.

* At 700 AM CST, a strong thunderstorm capable of producing
waterspouts was located 26 nm southwest of Oriskany Reef, or 29 nm
south of Perdido Pass, moving west at 10 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

* The strong thunderstorm will remain over mainly open waters.

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall will be possible,
especially over the western half of San Luis Valley.

* WHERE...The western half of the San Luis Valley, including
Antonito, Del Norte, Monte Vista and Alamosa.

* WHEN...From 5 PM MST this afternoon through late Tuesday night.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone location.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Runoff from heavy rain and melting snow over the San Juan
Mountains may cause flooding in the San Luis Valley, especially
Monday and Tuesday as high flows move out of the mountains and
through the Rio Grande and Conejos River.
- The greatest risk of flooding will be along the Conejos River and
the Rio Grande, including Del Norte, Monte Vista and Alamosa.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood http://cotrip.org

following areas, the Eastern San Juan Mountains, and the Upper Rio
Grande Valley.

* WHEN...Through Monday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone location.

and Highway 17 will likely be significantly impacted by this storm.

Mogote.

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Yavapai County in west central Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 245 PM MST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of creeks and normally dry washes is imminent or
occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 545 AM MST, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain. Flooding is
ongoing or expected to begin shortly in the warned area. Between
1.5 and 2.25 inches of rain have fallen.
- This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Ash Creek, Willow Creek, Miller Creek, Lynx Creek, Butte Creek,
Turkey Creek, Wolf Creek, Little Chino Valley, Big Bug Creek,
Agua Fria River, Bottleneck Wash, Milk Creek, Granite Creek,
Verde River, Bannon Creek and Hassayampa River. Additional
rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are possible in the warned
area.
- For Granite Creek at Prescott:
At 5:30am the stage was 11.0 feet.
Flood Stage is 11.0 feet.
Impacts:
At 11.0 feet: Flooding begins at AC Williams Granite Creek Park
upstream of gage. Low lying patios along Granite Creek in
downtown Prescott flood.
- For Granite Creek at Granite Creek Near Prescott:
At 5:30am the stage was 9.7 feet.
Flood Stage is 11.0 feet.
Forecast: A crest of 10.91 feet is expected at 6:00pm Sunday.
Impacts:
At 11.0 feet: Minor flooding. Lowland overflow. Bridge at
Industrial Way overtopped. Trails and bridges in Watson Woods
Riparian Preserve inundated.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Prescott, Chino Valley, Ponderosa Park, Groom Creek, Downtown
Prescott, Potato Patch, Oak Knoll Village, Whipple, Palace
Station, Wildwood Estates, Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University,
Prescott Regional Airport, Prescott Rodeo Grounds, Rancho Vista
Estates, Mt. Union, Goldwater Lake, Willow Creek Reservoir and
Watson Lake.
- This includes the following highways...
State Route 69 between mile markers 293 and 296. State Route 89
between mile markers 303 and 321...and near mile marker 331.
State Route 89A between mile markers 318 and 321.

This includes the following recreation areas andcampgrounds...
White Spar Campground, Upper Wolf Creek Group Campground, Lower
Wolf Creek Campground, Wolf Creek Falls, Acker Park, AC Williams
Granite Creek Park, Watson Lake Park and Goldwater Lake Park.

This includes the following swimming holes...
Wolf Creek Falls.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.
